In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. refutes.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` reports every diagnostic whose location is not in source (`!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource`). Metadata members now get a null location from `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` or `FirstOrDefault()`, which becomes `Location.None`. So MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004, an Error per L2) and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull are still reported in the consuming project, with no location, whenever the referenced type has such a problem. This contradicts L8, which says referenced types are deliberately not diagnosed. It also contradicts the two docs added by this change (README and MsgPack004.md), which say such members are reported only by the defining project. A user consuming a package built without the MessagePack analyzer would get a location-less error they cannot fix.
